note: Bundled public examples. 'expected' is the author's intent; only a recorded run establishes what the verifier observed. Splits: showcase is curated for demonstration; development informs prompts and implementation. Nothing here is held out.

examples.title: Queue that overwrites when full
examples.brief: A 4-entry, 8-bit FIFO for a UART receive path. Bytes must come out in the order they arrived. When the FIFO is full, new bytes are dropped rather than overwriting stored ones. Reset clears the FIFO.

examples.title: Known-good control (count style)
examples.brief: A 4-entry, 8-bit synchronous FIFO with synchronous active-high reset. Writes when full and reads when empty are ignored.

examples.title: Accepts a write when full and reading
examples.brief: A 4-entry FIFO. If it is full and a read and write arrive together, it should still accept the write because the read frees a slot.

examples.title: Bypasses a write to a read while empty
examples.brief: A 2-entry FIFO for a command queue.

examples.title: Reset forgets the write pointer
examples.brief: A 4-entry FIFO that may be reset at any time during operation.

examples.title: Reports full one word early
examples.brief: A 4-entry FIFO that should hold exactly four bytes.

examples.title: Read pointer loses its wrap bit
examples.brief: A 4-entry FIFO used continuously, so its pointers wrap many times.

examples.title: Duplicates a word on simultaneous read and write
examples.brief: A 4-entry streaming FIFO where reads and writes often happen in the same cycle.
